Subject: RFP commercial clarifications — commit tiers, overages, discounting (Ref: GTS RFP sec 5)

Diego,

Thanks for the quick review of the RFP. Procurement has a handful of commercial clarifications on section 5 before we finalize the scoring. Please see questions below — concise answers preferred so we can include them in the submission matrix.

1) Token pricing: You list a single per‑token rate for "standard generation". Can you break out pricing by model family (small / medium / large / instruction tuned) and state per‑1k token USD rates for both prompt and completion directions?

2) Commits & discounts: RFP calls for three commit levels (base, preferred, enterprise). Provide the commit bands (monthly and annual commit in tokens), the discount off list at each band, and any minimum contract length to qualify for the discount. Also confirm whether discounts can be stacked with multi‑year commitments.

3) Overage treatment: How are overages billed within a billing period? Is there a stepped overage ladder (e.g., 0–10% at list, 10–30% at +X%), or a flat overage price? Any grace bands or carryforward credits?

4) True‑up cadence: Do you support quarterly true‑ups or only annual true‑ups? What is the invoicing approach for shortfalls/overages?

5) Burst capacity & dedicated pools: If we specify a base commit but require predictable peak throughput, how are burst hours priced and guaranteed (dedicated capacity vs hosted burst)? Any separate pricing for guaranteed capacity?

6) Multi‑year pricing: Provide example pricing for a 2‑year and 3‑year committed scenario and indicate your early termination remedies/credits schedule.

7) Invoice terms & credits: Standard invoice terms, dispute window, and the process for crediting invoice adjustments.

Our timeline: answers by Monday PDT would be ideal so we can consolidate final RFP attachments.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the details.

Sara Lopez
Sourcing Manager, Greentech Solutions
procurement@greentech.com

Diego — quick notes inline on the spreadsheet and a recommended approach below.

1) Model family breakout (per 1k tokens):
- small (e.g., 4–6B): prompt $0.60 / 1k, completion $0.90 / 1k
- medium (13–20B): prompt $1.10 / 1k, completion $1.65 / 1k
- large (70–200B): prompt $3.50 / 1k, completion $5.25 / 1k
- instruction‑tuned / safety‑optimized variants: add 15% premium to the corresponding large rate.

2) Commit bands & discounts (monthly committed tokens equivalent):
- Base: 0–1.5B tokens/month — list pricing, 0% baseline discount
- Preferred: 1.5B–5B tokens/month — 10% discount off list
- Enterprise: >5B tokens/month — 20% discount off list
Minimum contract length to qualify: 12 months. Discounts stack with multi‑year (see below) but enterprise discounts are capped at a combined 25% total when combined with multi‑year incentives.

3) Overage: recommend stepped ladder to reduce churn risk — proposed ladder:
- 0–10% over commit: billed at discounted list (no penalty)
- 10–30% over: billed at list + 10% uplift
- >30% over: billed at list + 25% uplift; we recommend engaging for committed bump thereafter.
Grace band: one billing cycle per contract year where we allow up to 5% carryforward (positive or negative) to next quarter; true‑up reconciles annually.

4) True‑up cadence: quarterly usage reporting, annual contractual true‑up. Quarterly invoice adjustments allowed as credits/debits, but contractual true‑up and settlement annual.

5) Burst/dedicated pricing: hosted burst — free up to 10% of commit in average sustained minutes; guaranteed dedicated pools available as an add‑on: $X/hour per vGPU (we should keep $X as confidential in public RFP; spreadsheet includes numeric examples). Dedicated capacity requires a 3‑month lead time and an additional committed reservation contract.

6) Multi‑year: 2‑year: additional 8% on top of commit discount; 3‑year: additional 12% (subject to cap noted above). Early termination: pro‑rata repayment of multi‑year incentive over remaining months (standard).

7) Invoice terms: Net 30. Dispute window 60 days. Credits applied to next invoice unless requested as refund.

I'll annotate the sheet with numeric examples — suggest we include two sample decks: (A) 12‑month, 1.8B/mo preferred band; (B) 36‑month, 6B/mo enterprise band.

— Karthik
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference

Sara / Aaron — thanks for the questions and the fast timeline. Please find concise answers below and attached a clean PDF we will include in the RFP appendix plus an example pricing workbook. If you'd like, we can convert the spreadsheet rows into the RFP table format and return a clean PDF by EOD Monday.

Executive summary (short): Redwood offers per‑model family token rates, three commit bands with defined discounts, a stepped overage ladder with a small grace band, quarterly reporting with annual contractual true‑up, and multi‑year incentives. Dedicated guaranteed pools are available as a priced add‑on.

Q1 — Model family pricing (USD per 1k tokens):
- Small (4–6B): prompt $0.60, completion $0.90
- Medium (13–20B): prompt $1.10, completion $1.65
- Large (70–200B): prompt $3.50, completion $5.25
- Instruction/safety tuned variants: +15% uplift to the corresponding model family rate

Q2 — Commits & discounts (monthly tokens, discount off list):
- Base: 0–1.5B / month — 0% discount (list)
- Preferred: 1.5B–5B / month — 10% discount
- Enterprise: >5B / month — 20% discount
Minimum commitment length: 12 months. Multi‑year incentives: 2‑year +8%, 3‑year +12% (note: combined discounts capped at 25% total). Examples are in the attached workbook.

Q3 — Overage treatment:
- 0–10% over commit: billed at the discounted list price (no uplift)
- 10–30% over: billed at list +10% uplift
- >30% over: billed at list +25% uplift; at this point we generally recommend a committed increase to avoid sustained overage uplifts
Grace/Carryforward: one billing cycle per contract year up to 5% carryforward (positive or negative).

Q4 — True‑up cadence & invoicing:
- Quarterly usage reporting (token level) with monthly invoices. Annual contractual true‑up settles any shortfalls/credits. Quarterly invoice adjustments may be applied as credits or debits; final contractual settlement occurs at the annual true‑up.

Q5 — Burst & dedicated pools:
- Hosted burst: included up to an average of 10% of monthly commit; sustained peaks beyond that billed under overage ladder.
- Dedicated guaranteed pools: priced as a reservation (see workbook) and require ~3 months lead time. Reserved capacity provides guaranteed throughput and a separate SLA.

Q6 — Multi‑year pricing examples and termination:
- Example A (12 months, Preferred — 1.8B/mo): effective combined discount = 10% (preferred) => see sheet row A for numeric monthly invoices.
- Example B (36 months, Enterprise — 6B/mo): enterprise 20% + 3yr incentive 12% = 32% but capped at 25% effective max. Early termination: pro‑rata repayment of multi‑year incentive (straight‑line) for remaining term; usage true‑ups still apply.

Q7 — Invoice terms & credits:
- Net 30. Dispute window 60 days. Credits apply to next invoice by default; refunds accommodated on request. We provide tokenized usage detail for audit up to 12 months.
